intents.name: greeting
intents.response: Hello! I can help with questions about your mortgage Agreement in Principle (AIP). What would you like to know?

intents.name: what_is_aip
examples: what is an agreement in principle
what does decision in principle mean
what is a mortgage in principle
why do I need an aip
is an aip a mortgage offer
does an agreement in principle guarantee a mortgage
intents.response: An Agreement in Principle (AIP) is an early indication of how much we could lend you, based on your income and commitments. It isn't a mortgage offer: that comes after a full application and a property valuation.

intents.name: credit_score_impact
examples: does this affect my credit score
will an aip harm my credit rating
is this a hard credit search
will it show on my credit file
does applying hurt my credit score
intents.response: Getting an AIP here uses a soft search, which doesn't affect your credit score and isn't visible to other lenders. A hard search only happens when you make a full mortgage application.

intents.name: how_much_can_i_borrow
examples: how much could I borrow on my salary
how much will you lend me
how much mortgage can I afford
I earn 45000 how much can I borrow
how big a loan can I get
intents.response: As a guide, we lend up to 4.5 times your annual income, subject to your existing commitments. Tell me your annual income (for example "I earn £45,000") for an estimate, or use the form above for a full decision.

intents.name: documents_needed
examples: what proof of income do you need
what do I need to apply
which documents for a full application
intents.response: You don't need any documents for an AIP. For a full application you'll usually need photo ID, proof of address, your last 3 months' payslips and 3 months' bank statements.

intents.name: aip_validity
examples: how long is my aip valid
when does the agreement in principle expire
how long does an aip last
how many days is it valid for
intents.response: Your AIP is valid for 90 days. If it expires before you apply, you can simply get a new one.

intents.name: referred_meaning
intents.response: "Referred" means we can't give an instant answer, often because the loan is above 4.5 times your income or more checks are needed. An underwriter will review it. It isn't a decline.

intents.name: declined_next_steps
examples: what can I do if I am declined
how can I improve my chances after a decline
can I reapply after being declined
why did I get turned down
intents.response: A decline is usually because existing credit commitments are high compared to income. Reducing commitments or borrowing less may help. You can reapply any time, and an advisor can talk it through with you.

intents.name: deposit_ltv
examples: how much deposit do I need
can I get a mortgage with a 5 percent deposit
intents.response: Loan to value (LTV) is the loan as a percentage of the property's value. We lend up to 90% LTV, so you'd need at least a 10% deposit. A bigger deposit can mean better rates.

intents.name: speak_to_advisor
examples: can I speak to an advisor
I want to talk to a human
I need to talk to an agent
intents.response: Of course. I'll pass you to a mortgage advisor. Please call 0800 000 0000 (Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm) or request a call back from your account.

intents.name: complaint
examples: I want to make a complaint
I am unhappy with the service
I want to raise a complaint
intents.response: I'm sorry you're unhappy. I'll pass you to a colleague who can help with your complaint. Please call 0800 000 0000.

intents.name: thanks_goodbye
intents.response: You're welcome. Good luck with your home search!

fallback.response: Sorry, I can only help with questions about your Agreement in Principle. You can rephrase, or ask to speak to an advisor.
